mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.05% for 3 consecutive months signals an imminent monetary easing cycle, which increases the present value of future equity cash flows by reducing the discount rate applied to them, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for 3 consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, which reduces the marginal productivity of capital and lowers the real wage growth rate, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in labor market weakness periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the GDP deflator inflation rate below 2% for 3 consecutive months signals a disinflationary trend, which reduces the real risk-free rate and lowers the cost of capital, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in disinflationary periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index above 105% of its 2019 average for 3 consecutive months signals a strengthening demand cycle, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and equity valuations, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in demand strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the housing starts index above 1.2 million units for 3 consecutive months signals an expansionary monetary policy, which increases the liquidity in the financial system and reduces the cost of capital, thereby producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in monetary expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the producer price index above 2.5% for 3 consecutive months signals a supply-side inflationary pressure, which increases the real risk-free rate and raises the cost of capital, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in supply-side inflation periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index above 3% for 3 consecutive months signals a labor market tightness, which increases the marginal productivity of capital and raises the real wage growth rate, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in labor market tightness periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the personal consumption expenditures deflator inflation rate above 2.5% for 3 consecutive months signals a monetary tightening cycle, which increases the real risk-free rate and raises the cost of capital, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in monetary tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
